claim_judgments.rationale: C0000 accurately captures the general prohibition in 14 CFR 91.213(a) against taking off an aircraft with inoperative instruments or equipment unless the paragraph (a) conditions are met, preserving the exception for operations under paragraph (d).
C0001 faithfully represents condition (a)(1) requiring the existence of an approved Minimum Equipment List for the aircraft, correctly inheriting the governing takeoff scope from paragraph (a).
C0002 correctly states condition (a)(2) requiring the aircraft to have within it a letter of authorization issued by the responsible Flight Standards office authorizing operation under the MEL.
C0003 correctly reflects the permission in paragraph (a)(2) that the letter of authorization may be obtained by written request of the airworthiness certificate holder.
C0004 correctly captures the legal definition/statement in paragraph (a)(2) that the MEL and letter of authorization constitute a supplemental type certificate for the aircraft.
C0005 accurately represents paragraph (a)(3), retaining both conditions: compliance with paragraph (b) limitations and providing for operation with instruments/equipment in an inoperable condition.
C0006 accurately states condition (a)(4) that aircraft records available to the pilot must include an entry describing the inoperable instruments and equipment.
C0007 correctly captures condition (a)(5) requiring operation under all applicable conditions and limitations in the MEL and authorizing letter.

C0008 accurately captures all three items in paragraph (b) that may not be included in a Minimum Equipment List, including airworthiness requirements, airworthiness directives, and part-specific operating rules.
C0009 correctly captures the mandate of paragraph (c) requiring specified authorized persons under subpart K, part 121, 125, or 135 to use their approved MEL to comply with § 91.213.

C0010 fully and faithfully captures the permission to take off without an MEL under paragraph (d) together with all four cumulative conditions: eligible aircraft types, excluded instrument/equipment categories, removal or placarding/deactivation, and the hazard determination.

C0011 correctly represents the requirement in paragraph (d)(3)(ii) that if deactivation of inoperative instruments/equipment involves maintenance, it must be accomplished and recorded in accordance with part 43.

C0012 accurately captures the legal status statement following paragraph (d)(4) regarding an aircraft with inoperative instruments/equipment being in a properly altered condition acceptable to the Administrator.
C0013 accurately reflects paragraph (e), permitting operation of an aircraft with inoperable instruments/equipment under a special flight permit notwithstanding any other provision of § 91.213.

unit_judgments.rationale: C0000 completely and accurately captures the prohibition on takeoff without meeting conditions (1) through (5) or qualifying under paragraph (d).
C0001 preserves the requirement under paragraph (a)(1) that an approved MEL must exist for the aircraft.
C0002 covers the requirement of paragraph (a)(2) for the aircraft to carry a letter of authorization issued by Flight Standards.
C0003 covers the permission in paragraph (a)(2) for the airworthiness certificate holder to obtain the letter of authorization by written request.
C0004 covers the legal provision that the MEL and LOA constitute a supplemental type certificate.
C0005 explicitly includes the requirement from paragraph (a)(3)(i) that the MEL must be prepared in accordance with paragraph (b) limitations.
C0005 explicitly includes the requirement from paragraph (a)(3)(ii) that the MEL must provide for operation with instruments and equipment in an inoperable condition.
C0006 covers the requirement of paragraph (a)(4) that aircraft records available to the pilot must include an entry describing inoperable equipment.
C0007 covers the requirement of paragraph (a)(5) that the aircraft is operated under all conditions and limitations in the MEL and authorizing letter.
C0008 fully retains the exclusion of airworthiness/safety-essential items from an MEL under paragraph (b)(1).
C0008 fully retains the exclusion of AD-mandated operable items from an MEL under paragraph (b)(2), preserving the exception where the AD provides otherwise.
C0008 fully retains the exclusion of items required for specific operations under part 91 from an MEL under paragraph (b)(3).
C0009 fully retains the duty in paragraph (c) for authorized operators under subpart K, part 121, 125, or 135 to use their approved MEL.
C0010 fully retains the permission and governing qualifications under paragraph (d)(1)(i) for takeoff without an MEL in aircraft without a master minimum equipment list.
C0010 fully retains the permission and governing qualifications under paragraph (d)(1)(ii) for takeoff without an MEL in aircraft for which an MMEL has been developed.
C0010 incorporates condition (d)(2)(i) requiring that inoperative instruments and equipment are not part of VFR-day type certification requirements.
C0010 incorporates condition (d)(2)(ii) requiring that inoperative items are not indicated as required on equipment lists or KOEL.
C0010 incorporates condition (d)(2)(iii) requiring that inoperative items are not required by § 91.205 or other part 91 operating rules.
C0010 incorporates condition (d)(2)(iv) requiring that inoperative items are not required to be operational by an airworthiness directive.
C0010 incorporates alternative condition (d)(3)(i) regarding removal, cockpit control placarding, and § 43.9 maintenance recording.
C0010 and C0011 jointly and fully cover condition (d)(3)(ii) regarding deactivation, placarding 'Inoperative', and part 43 maintenance recording.
C0010 incorporates condition (d)(4) requiring a hazard determination by a certificated pilot or maintenance person.
C0012 covers the statement that an aircraft operating under paragraph (d) is considered to be in a properly altered condition acceptable to the Administrator.
C0013 covers the authorization under paragraph (e) to operate under a special flight permit in accordance with §§ 21.197 and 21.199.
